content_preview.title: Ollama 0.40.2 Upgrades Downloaded Models in the Background and Keeps Backups, 0.40.3 Pauses It, and 0.40.4 Adds Decision Models to ollama run
content_preview.summary: Ollama's v0.40.2 release notes say older models are upgraded in the background with backups kept on disk; v0.40.3 pauses the upgrade, and v0.40.4 adds decision models to the CLI.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Three Ollama releases published between October 8 and October 12, 2026 changed how the local-model runner handles models that users already have on disk and added a new way to query them. According to the [v0.40.2 release notes](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.40.2), models downloaded with earlier versions are upgraded in the background the first time they are run, with the original copy kept as a backup. editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News article (690 words by raw count and with link URLs stripped; News range 400-1200). Title is 141 characters (cap 150). Structure: overview, per-release sections, background, explicit unknowns. Everything is attributed to Ollama's own release notes and the article says so; no independent testing is claimed.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four gzipped snapshots (source-0..3.html.gz) and extracted the release body from each; none is page chrome only, each contains the full release notes (markdown-body present). manifest suspicious_patterns is null for all four, status 200, no archive fallback. source-0 (v0.40.2): 'Models downloaded with earlier versions of Ollama are upgraded in the background the first time you run them, for better performance and compatibility when running on llama.cpp.' (verbatim match to the article quote); 'To make downgrading safe, Ollama keeps the original copy as a backup, so upgraded models are temporarily kept on disk. A future release will remove these backups automatically.' (supports 'Keeps Backups'); jq snippet; 'This only deletes the backups. If you later downgrade to a version older than 0.40, you'll need to re-pull those models.'; 'ollama list no longer shows duplicate entries for upgraded models'; 'ollama launch claude uses the model's full context length'. All match. source-1 (v0.40.3): exactly three bullets (Claude connectors warning removed, codex service tiers warning removed, 'Paused background model upgrade for embedding and other request performance, by @jmorganca in #18908'); quote matches. The line states the upgrade was paused with no conditions or scope given; it does not say whether the pause is temporary or what requests were affected, as the article states. Title 'Pauses It' is therefore a faithful gloss of the notes' flat wording; the article body keeps the caveat. source-2 (v0.40.4): headline 'Decision models in the CLI ... directly from the terminal with ollama run - ask yes/no questions, classify text into labels, or score against a rubric' and the nimble example match; 'Kev decision models are now supported by the MLX runner on Apple silicon' (undefined term; article quotes it as written and lists it under unknowns; the title does not assert what 'Kev' means); 'Updated llama.cpp with native decision model support'; codex model picker, usage credits, multimodal embeddings, Gemma 4 prefill, 'improved' items with no figures: all match. Confirmed absences: v0.40.4 notes do not mention backups, the pause, or the upgrade; v0.40.3 notes do not say the pause is temporary or whether the upgrade resumed; v0.40.2 notes give no disk-size estimate or removal date beyond 'a future release'. source-3 (v0.40.0): 'Decision models are now available on MLX as well: Nimble tev1 clef clef-flash' and MLX-by-default on Apple Silicon match. Zero occurrences of 'OpenAI' across all four snapshots, so the article's statement that the Ollama notes do not mention OpenAI is correct. GitHub API: v0.40.0 published 2026-09-25T03:31:52Z (updated 10-06); v0.40.2 2026-10-08T16:53:47Z; v0.40.3 2026-10-11T01:39:04Z; v0.40.4 2026-10-12T19:00:12Z (updated_at 2026-10-14T02:23:26Z). All article dates (Sept 25, Oct 8, 11, 12) match and no later v0.40.x release exists. Live re-fetch of the v0.40.4 body via the GitHub API on 2026-10-14 compared with the snapshot: same items and wording, no substantive change. All four snapshots exist and contain real release text; none missing.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific (versions, dates, command, product names Nimble/tev1/clef/clef-flash, quotes) traces to the cited release notes. The headline's three claims are each supported: backups and background upgrade (v0.40.2), upgrade paused (v0.40.3), decision models in ollama run (v0.40.4). Nuance: the title says 'Pauses It' flatly while the notes tie the pause to embedding and other request performance; the body states this and the unknowns list covers resumption. 'Adds Decision Models to ollama run' is the notes' own headline. Vendor claims (better performance, improved) are attributed to Ollama and no numbers are invented.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributive, no hype; notes absence of figures.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Ollama release-notes article in the archive; only Copilot CLI Ollama model discovery (10-08) and unrelated pieces mention Ollama. New topic.
editor_notes.internal_link_check: The link /article/2026-10/09-openai-puts-decisions-api-in-beta-returning-probabilities-and-scores-from-gpt-6-luna-at-010-per-million-input-tokens resolves to an existing published article (singular /article/ form, slug matches the file exactly). I read it: it covers OpenAI's hosted Decisions API (gpt-6-luna, /v1/decisions) and a Perplexity Decider on OpenRouter. It could lead a reader to infer a connection to Ollama's locally run decision models. The article mitigates this by saying the Ollama notes never mention OpenAI and that it does not treat the two as related; I judge that adequate, as the link signals a shared product category and not a relationship.
